title: Microscopic Mechanism and Control of Reentrant Localization
authors: Pei-Jie Chang, Quanfeng Lu, Wentao Yang, Dong Ruan, Gui-Lu Long
abstract: Increasing quasiperiodic modulation can restore extended states after localization, raising the question of how the same modulation drives both localization and recovery. We identify a microscopic mechanism in quasiperiodic dimer chains by resolving scattering between Fourier channels. Specifically, scattering into neighboring channels and back shifts the spectral edge relative to a localization boundary determined by a neutral auxiliary resonance. Their successive crossings drive the same spectral packet with fixed integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels into localization and back into an extended regime. This recovery persists across finite parameter ranges in both gap-opening families, including relative-phase detuning. Furthermore, an exact sublattice mapping enables compensated control of the recovery window and predicts recovery thresholds for individual IDS labels.
summary: This theoretical work elucidates the mechanism behind reentrant localization in quasiperiodic dimer chains, showing that the process is governed by the relative crossing of spectral edges and resonance boundaries. By employing an exact sublattice mapping, the authors demonstrate a method to actively control the parameter regime where extended states are recovered, providing precise thresholds for this phenomenon.
main_problem: The paper investigates the microscopic mechanism and control of 'reentrant localization' in quasiperiodic systems, where the modulation causing localization can subsequently restore extended states.
main_result: Reentrance is driven by the successive crossing of the spectral edge (from Fourier scattering) relative to a localization boundary set by a neutral auxiliary resonance. Furthermore, compensated sublattice modulation allows for the precise control of the recovery window.
method: The analysis combines spectral theory (using self-energy calculations and spectral edge tracking) with real-space diagnostics like the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) and growth rate analysis.
model_or_system: The system is a quasiperiodic dimer chain described by a Hamiltonian involving onsite potentials modulated by a quasiperiodic function $	heta_m$. The analysis maps this to a dual chain of coupled momentum channels and an auxiliary-chain eigen-problem.
key_observables: Integrated Density of States (IDS) packets, spectral edge ($e_{gM}$), neutral resonance boundary ($e_{bR}$), and the relative motion $\Delta M, R = e_{gM} - e_{bR}$.
important_parameters: Modulation strength ($\lambda$), relative phase ($\delta$), and the modulation control parameter ($\eta$) used for sublattice compensation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to an auxiliary chain and assumes that the recovery mechanism can be controlled by manipulating the sublattice modulation potentials.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral-edge motion relative to the neutral resonance, mapping out regions of reentrant recovery, and showing the dependence of participation exponents on the control parameter $\eta$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem using the dimer chain Hamiltonian, develops the theoretical framework by mapping to Fourier channels and auxiliary resonances, and then details the control mechanism using compensated sublattice modulation to predict and confirm recovery thresholds for specific IDS labels.
why_interesting: The concept of reentrant behavior—where a parameter drives a system through multiple distinct phases (localized $	o$ extended $	o$ localized $	o$ extended)—is highly relevant to understanding complex many-body dynamics in disordered or quasiperiodic media.
